audit_findings.title: Growth-related working-capital investment may be omitted from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $210.5 million 2025 increase in net trade working capital, equal to 16.8% of the $1,254.9 million OE anchor; normalized valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE anchor and projected 6%-8% growth do not explicitly deduct the receivables and inventory investment required to support growth, increasing projected OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: A third factor that tends to require incremental inventory increases over time is our growth drivers, including our FMI offerings, customer contract signings, and international expansion, all of which tend to require significant investments in inventory.
audit_findings.explanation: The model omission is demonstrated: the anchor is approximately net income, while the filing shows that 2025 growth required a $210.5 million increase in net trade working capital. That annual amount cannot automatically be treated as normalized, but its scale relative to the anchor and the base case's 51.5% terminal-value share makes the unresolved normalization reasonably capable of materially changing intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to net income, D&A, maintenance capex, and operating working-capital changes; derive a normalized incremental working-capital requirement from filed multi-year data and rerun every growth scenario with that reinvestment explicitly funded.

audit_findings.title: Deferred 2025 capital spending may inflate the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 net capex was $4.4-$24.4 million below the filed $235-$255 million range; the maximum shortfall equals 1.9% of the OE anchor and approximately $0.35 per share if treated as a permanent base-case OE reduction
audit_findings.mechanism: Any deferred maintenance or replacement spending would reduce normalized OE; growth and efficiency capital would not reduce maintenance-based OE in the same manner.
audit_findings.evidence: We were below our anticipated range due to delayed projects that are expected to resume in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The deferral is demonstrated, but the filed range bounds the entire 2025 shortfall at $24.4 million. Even the conservative assumption that all of that amount represents recurring maintenance would reduce the base value by only about 1.9%, far smaller than the 30% margin of safety and the $31.43 gap between the $49.595 market price and $18.17 base value. The maintenance portion is necessarily smaller than or equal to that bound.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the 2026 project-level capex schedule, classify the deferred Atlanta, trucking, IT, replacement, capacity, and efficiency expenditures, and confirm that recurring maintenance does not exceed the bounded shortfall before closing the item.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor precedes the full tariff cost burden
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $20.6 million pretax H1 2026 unfavorable net price/cost effect computed as 45 basis points of $4,588.6 million sales; the filed tariff and import-shipping net-income effect remained immaterial and any later burden is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An unoffset tariff-driven increase in inventory cost would reduce gross margin, forward OE, and terminal value after lower-tariff inventory is exhausted.
audit_findings.evidence: We estimate the effect on our net income related to tariffs and import shipping cost s was immaterial in 2025; however, our tariff exposure may become more impactful in subsequent quarters as our lower tariff inventory is depleted and replaced with inventory that is subject to new and expanded tariffs.
audit_findings.explanation: The warned-about future exposure is not yet demonstrated as a material earnings loss. H1 2026 showed approximately 45 basis points of unfavorable net price/cost, but the filing still characterized the tariff and import-shipping effect on net income as immaterial; operating margin nevertheless increased to 20.7% from 20.5%. The possible later burden remains forward-looking and should be monitored rather than treated as a presently quantified anchor error.
audit_findings.action: Compare quarterly realized pricing, landed inventory cost, gross margin, and tariff refunds through the completion of inventory turnover; rerun forward OE if cumulative price recovery fails to offset replacement-inventory costs.

audit_findings.title: Cash may not be fully distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum bridge exposure of $204.7 million, equal to approximately $0.18 per share and 1.0% of the $21,007 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Operationally required, inaccessible, or tax-burdened cash should be excluded from the equity bridge rather than added dollar-for-dollar.
audit_findings.evidence: Accordingly, no deferred taxes have been provided for withholding taxes or other taxes that would result upon repatriation of our approximately $ 625.3 of undistributed income from foreign subsidiaries to the U.S. as that income continues to be permanently reinvested.
audit_findings.explanation: Accessibility of the June 2026 cash is unresolved, but even removing the entire $204.7 million bridge addition would lower base value only from $18.17 to approximately $17.99 per share. That cannot materially affect the conclusion relative to the $49.595 market price or the 30% margin of safety. The $625.3 million of undistributed foreign income is not itself the cash balance and does not enlarge the bridge exposure.
audit_findings.action: Identify cash by jurisdiction and minimum operating requirement, estimate any repatriation friction, and replace the bridge amount with demonstrably accessible surplus cash; no full valuation rerun is needed unless another bridge asset is identified.

audit_findings.title: A discrete tax benefit may remain in the recurring anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $8.3 million anchor reduction computed as 0.5% of $1,655.0 million 2025 pretax income, producing approximately a $0.12 per-share reduction in the base valuation
audit_findings.mechanism: Using the reported 24.0% tax rate instead of the disclosed 24.5% ongoing rate increases recurring after-tax OE and its terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We believe our ongoing tax rate, absent any discrete tax items or broader changes to tax law, will be approximately 24.5%.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a 0.5 percentage-point difference between the reported and ongoing tax rates, although the record does not establish whether the valuation separately removed it. Assuming no removal, the correction is only about 0.7% of the OE anchor and about $0.12 per base-case share, which is immaterial relative to the margin of safety and market-price gap.
audit_findings.action: Recast 2025 OE at the disclosed 24.5% ongoing tax rate, document removal of the $7.4 million favorable change in unrecognized tax benefits and other discrete items, and confirm the resulting approximately $8.3 million adjustment.

audit_findings.title: Vehicle residual-value guarantees are an unbridged contingent senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $124.2 million maximum disclosed guarantee, equal to approximately $0.11 per share and 0.6% of base equity value; expected loss unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any vehicle-value shortfall funded under the guarantee would be an additional cash claim ahead of common equity and would reduce OE or the equity bridge when incurred or estimable.
audit_findings.evidence: The aggregate residual value guarantee related to these leases was approximately $ 124.2 .
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q confirms that the $124.2 million guarantee and management's remote-loss assessment are unchanged, so no present liability or demonstrated valuation error exists. Even the full face amount is small relative to base equity value, but the guarantee remains a forward-looking tripwire because realized loss depends on vehicle values and contractual settlement terms.
audit_findings.action: Monitor each filing for changes in the $124.2 million exposure or remote-loss assessment and obtain current vehicle fair values, contractual floors, and historical settlement losses; rerun the bridge only if a probable or reasonably estimable shortfall emerges.
